summary: Israel eliminated two senior Hamas operatives in northern Gaza, including a weapons production commander and a Nukhba force member, while simultaneously striking Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon. Iran announced a halt to retaliatory attacks against the U.S. contingent on no further American strikes, as diplomatic efforts via Oman reportedly paused U.S. operations in Iran. Syria's president expressed willingness for a security agreement with Israel, signaling a potential regional realignment.
key_points: IDF killed Hamas weapons production chief Fares al-Masri and Nukhba operative Mohammad Abu Shakian in northern Gaza strikes last Tuesday, citing violations of ceasefire and threat removal. (Source: @New_security8200/202988)
Iranian military declared suspension of retaliatory attacks provided the U.S. refrains from further strikes on Iran, per Al Arabiya. (Source: @pkpoi/143451)

U.S. Ambassador to UN Mike Waltz stated Trump is offering diplomacy with Iran, while CBS reported U.S. strikes in Iran halted after Omani mediation. (Source: @New_security8200/202997, @yediotnews25/133232)
Iranian leader Mojtaba Khamenei set defense of Hezbollah and full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon as preconditions for any agreement to end the "imposed war" with the U.S. (Source: @asafroz/51928)

Israeli forces engaged a Hezbollah surveillance drone over their positions in Lebanon, while heavy strikes hit five southern Lebanese villages including Bint Jbeil and Mais al-Jabal. (Source: @naya_foriraq/85673, @rodast_omiddana/77776)
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa told Al Jazeera his government seeks a security agreement with Israel mediated by a group of countries and avoids confrontation. (Source: @New_security8200/202994)
Yemen's armed forces attacked three Saudi tankers in 48 hours, with 16 Saudi vessels diverted since Monday, per Al Mayadeen. (Source: @SharghDaily/174581)

CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper advised halting the Strait of Hormuz bombing campaign, assessing it had degraded Iran's ship-targeting capability and eliminated most designated targets. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5760)

sections.executive_summary: Israel conducted precision strikes in northern Gaza eliminating Hamas weapons production commander Fares al-Masri and Nukhba operative Mohammad Abu Shakian, while expanding air operations against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. Iran declared a conditional pause in retaliatory attacks against U.S. forces, coinciding with Omani diplomatic efforts that reportedly halted American strikes inside Iran. Simultaneously, Syria's new leadership signaled openness to a security arrangement with Israel, and Yemen escalated maritime pressure on Saudi shipping, indicating a fluid multi-theater dynamic.

points: Iran's military announced a halt to retaliatory attacks against the United States on condition that Washington refrains from further strikes on Iranian territory, according to Al Arabiya reporting. (Source: @pkpoi/143451)

Mojtaba Khamenei, in a published message, declared the defense of Hezbollah as Iran's strategic policy and set the preservation of Lebanon's territorial integrity and a complete, unconditional cessation of Israeli aggression as the first condition for any agreement to end the "imposed war" with the United States. (Source: @asafroz/51928, @yediotnews25/133239)

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi condemned the Ukrainian strike on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea as a "clear violation of the UN Charter" that "cannot go unanswered," alleging President Zelensky acted at Israel's behest to draw Europe into war, and discussed the matter with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. (Source: @VahidOnline/77510)

Iranian lawmaker Ebrahim Azizi warned that Ukraine may "soon understand" Tehran does not leave hostile actions unanswered, stating the list of countries that have miscalculated Iran's response "continues to grow." (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5773)

The IRGC Aerospace Force is reportedly preparing retaliation for the Ukrainian SBU attack on an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea using one-way attack drones, with the distance noted as approximately 1,850 kilometers. (Source: @kianmeli1/90111)

U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said President Trump is giving an opportunity for diplomacy with Iran, while CBS reported U.S. strikes in Iran were halted after Omani officials arrived in Tehran for mediation talks on Friday. (Source: @New_security8200/202997, @yediotnews25/133232)

CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper recommended stopping the bombing campaign around the Strait of Hormuz, assessing it had reached the limit of its effectiveness after significantly reducing Iran's ability to target ships and eliminating most designated targets; he noted 20% of targets from "Hamaseh Ghazab" operations remain if large-scale operations resume. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5760, @VahidOnline/77511)

The IDF confirmed the elimination of Hamas weapons production commander Fares al-Masri and Nukhba operative Mohammad Abu Shakian in separate strikes in northern Gaza last Tuesday, stating both were advancing terror attacks against Israeli forces and civilians in violation of the ceasefire. (Source: @New_security8200/202988, @manniefabian/58862)
Israeli forces opened fire on a Hezbollah surveillance drone carrying a camera over their positions in Lebanon, according to Israeli Army Radio. (Source: @naya_foriraq/85673)

Prime Minister Netanyahu told Senator Lindsey Graham during "Lion's Roar" discussions that Israel is focused on Iran, and that if Hezbollah is told Israel will go "all the way," they will have no choice but to go all the way, but added "currently we don't want that." (Source: @inon_yttach/9680)

Heavy Israeli airstrikes struck the southern Lebanese villages of Barashit, Bint Jbeil, Aitaroun, Al-Tiri, and Mais al-Jabal, described as "powerful attacks" occurring "right now." (Source: @rodast_omiddana/77776)

Reports from Gaza indicate an additional strike near a mosque in the Al-Tuffah neighborhood, and a separate double elimination of two Hamas commanders. (Source: @New_security8200/203003, @almogboker78/17825)

The Israeli cabinet approved in principle the entry of an International Stabilization Force (ISF) into Gaza under Trump's 20-point plan, but insisted the IDF will continue holding the "yellow line" with no withdrawal until Hamas is fully disarmed and Gaza fully demilitarized; any ISF deployment requires individual approval by the Prime Minister, Defense Minister, and Foreign Minister, limited to countries with peace agreements not acting against Israel, initially about 200 personnel from friendly states like Uganda and Morocco. (Source: @New_security8200/203001)
The Pentagon updated its official casualty database from the Iran war, adding a new "Overseas Operations" category for personnel killed or wounded since July 7. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5776)

IDF strikes in northern Gaza last Tuesday killed Hamas weapons production chief Fares al-Masri, head of a section in the Hamas weapons production headquarters, and Nukhba operative Mohammad Abu Shakian, both accused of working to rebuild Hamas capabilities and advance attacks on Israeli troops and civilians. (Source: @New_security8200/202988, @manniefabian/58862)

Hamas's Interior Ministry reported the killing of Wael al-Ladawi, head of the Internal Security Mechanism in the Central Governorate, and officer Ramz Abu Zrik in a vehicle strike in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. (Source: @New_security8200/202993)
Gaza sources reported an Israeli strike near a mosque in the Al-Tuffah neighborhood. (Source: @New_security8200/203003)
Additional reports from Gaza described a double elimination of two Hamas commanders in the Strip. (Source: @almogboker78/17825)

Israel's cabinet approved an International Stabilization Force (ISF) entry to Gaza per Trump's 20-point plan but maintained the IDF will hold the "yellow line" with no withdrawal until Hamas is fully disarmed and Gaza fully demilitarized; ISF operations beyond the yellow line require full coordination with the IDF and individual approval by the Prime Minister, Defense Minister, and Foreign Minister. (Source: @New_security8200/203001)

Mojtaba Khamenei declared Iran's strategic policy is the defense of Hezbollah, and set the preservation of Lebanon's territorial integrity and a complete, unconditional cessation of Israeli aggression as the first condition for any agreement to end the "imposed war" with the United States. sections.threat_assessment: The simultaneous Israeli kinetic operations in Gaza and Lebanon, coupled with Iran's conditional pause in retaliation and explicit linkage of Hezbollah's defense to any U.S. agreement, create a fragile equilibrium. Iran's threat to retaliate against Ukraine for the Caspian Sea strike, potentially using long-range one-way drones, introduces a new vector of escalation beyond the Middle East. Yemen's sustained maritime campaign against Saudi shipping demonstrates the Houthis' capacity to disrupt Gulf energy flows independently of the Iran-U.S. dynamic. Israel's insistence on maintaining the "yellow line" in Gaza and linking any international force to Hamas's complete disarmament suggests a prolonged military presence. The Syrian overture for a security agreement with Israel, if genuine, could alter northern border calculations but remains unverified on the ground.
sections.regional_response: Omani mediation appears to have achieved a temporary pause in direct U.S.-Iran strikes, with both sides signaling openness to diplomacy. The Gulf states, particularly Saudi Arabia, face continued Houthi pressure on shipping lanes, while the reported 16 diverted tankers indicate economic impact. Lebanon's government remains caught between Hezbollah's integration into Iranian strategy and Israeli military pressure on its southern villages. Syria's new leadership is testing diplomatic space with Israel, potentially seeking legitimacy and reconstruction aid. The international community's response to the Ukrainian strike on an Iranian vessel — and Iran's threatened retaliation — will test the coherence of Western policy toward both the Russia-Ukraine war and Iran's regional network.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Caspian Sea strike represents a significant expansion of Ukrainian targeting into Iran's rear logistics, specifically interdicting drone and missile components. Iran's public preparation for a ~1,850 km drone retaliation suggests a capability demonstration intended to deter further such attacks. The Pentagon's creation of an "Overseas Operations" casualty category since July 7 implies sustained, undeclared U.S. military activity in the region beyond the acknowledged Strait of Hormuz campaign. Israel's ISF framework, limited to 200 personnel from non-adversarial states with peace treaties, appears designed to facilitate humanitarian and stabilization tasks without compromising operational freedom. The reported elimination of Hamas's internal security chief in Deir al-Balah indicates Israeli intelligence penetration of Hamas's reorganized command structure in central Gaza.
